name: IRDAI Standard Non-Payable Consumables Catalog
authority: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) & General Insurance Council (GIC)
reference: IRDAI Master Circular on Standardization of Exclusions (Annexure I, List I - Expenses Not Admissible)

rules.explanation: Under IRDAI standardization guidelines, routine examination and surgical gloves are classified as non-payable consumables and typically deducted unless bundled into an all-inclusive surgical package rate.
rules.patient_remedy: Ask hospital billing desk for a surgical package itemization or doctor certificate confirming gloves were specialized and procedure-critical.

rules.guideline_reference: IRDAI List I - Item 2 (PPE & Protective Gear)
rules.explanation: Personal protective apparel including standard masks, caps, and PPE kits for staff are treated as hospital overhead consumables rather than patient-specific medical treatment charges.
rules.patient_remedy: If admission was in an isolated infectious disease ward or critical care ICU requiring specialized barrier nursing, obtain an ICU barrier nursing justification letter from the hospital.

rules.explanation: Disinfectant solutions and routine sanitizers used during ward rounds or nursing are considered general hospital hygiene maintenance expenses.
rules.patient_remedy: Only specialized wound debridement antiseptics prescribed directly by the surgeon on the operative record may be challenged for reconsideration.

rules.guideline_reference: IRDAI List I - Item 7 (Registration & Admission Fees)
rules.explanation: IRDAI guidelines state that administrative fees for patient registration, medical records (MRD), file folders, and admission processing cannot be passed on to health insurance claims.
rules.patient_remedy: These are strictly hospital administrative overheads under IRDAI regulations; hospitals are not permitted to bill these under reimbursable medical expenses.

rules.guideline_reference: IRDAI List I - Item 11 (Waste Management & Hospital Levies)
rules.explanation: Hospital bio-medical waste management and environmental compliance levies are institutional overheads and are excluded from health insurance claims.
rules.patient_remedy: Hospitals should absorb statutory waste compliance into room rent and cannot levy itemized patient surcharges under standard TPA guidelines.

rules.guideline_reference: IRDAI List I - Item 15 (Personal Comfort & Attendant Items)
rules.explanation: Services and amenities provided for the convenience of family members, visitors, or attendants are not medical treatments and are not covered.
rules.patient_remedy: These are non-medical attendant charges and must be borne out-of-pocket by the policyholder.

rules.guideline_reference: IRDAI List I - Item 21 (Non-medical food, mineral water & supplements)
rules.explanation: Commercial mineral water, visitor catering, and nutritional supplements not strictly certified as parenteral or critical clinical nutrition are excluded.
rules.patient_remedy: If enteral feeding or therapeutic clinical nutrition was medically mandated, obtain a clinical nutritionist prescription in the inpatient case notes.

rules.guideline_reference: IRDAI List I - Item 28 (General Reusable Instruments)
rules.explanation: General monitoring equipment and patient comfort appliances that are durable/reusable hospital assets are non-payable when billed individually.
rules.patient_remedy: If a respirometer or incentive spirometer was taken home for post-discharge pulmonary rehabilitation, claim under post-hospitalization rehabilitation benefits if your policy covers it.

rules.guideline_reference: IRDAI List I - Item 34 (Routine Dressing Materials)
rules.explanation: Routine wound dressing materials and adhesive tapes billed as itemized consumables outside surgical theater packages are routinely marked non-payable.
rules.patient_remedy: Request the treating surgeon to clarify if complex multi-layer burn/surgical wound dressing requiring specialized sterile packs was performed.

rules.guideline_reference: IRDAI List I - Item 42 (Personal Hygiene Items)
rules.explanation: Toiletry, sanitary pads, disposable underpads, and personal hygiene products are classified as non-medical daily living consumables.
rules.patient_remedy: These are personal hygiene items and must be settled directly by the policyholder.
